message.reasoning_content:
The image shows an Omega Speedmaster Professional with what appears to be a "racing" or "speedmaster reduced" dial? Let me look carefully.

The dial has three subdials: left at 9 o'clock shows 60/20/40 seconds (running seconds), right at 3 o'clock shows 30/10/20 minute counter, and the bottom at 6 o'clock shows 12/6/9? Actually the bottom subdial shows "12" at top? It shows "12" at top and "6" at bottom with "3" and "9"? Hmm, it says "9" bottom left and "12"? Actually there's a numbered 12-hour counter.

Wait — a standard Speedmaster Professional (Moonwatch) has subdials at 3, 6, 9: 30-minute counter at 3, 12-hour counter at 6, running seconds at 9. That matches.

The bracelet appears to be a metal bracelet — the "panda"? No, it's a black dial. The bracelet looks like... a "Speedy" bracelet? Actually the bracelet has a flat-link design, looks like the Speedmaster "President"-style? Hmm, the link design with rounded links resembles the Speedmaster Professional bracelet 1998 (1450/1479?). Actually it looks like the classic Speedmaster 1171 bracelet? Or perhaps a Speedy "Moonwatch" with the newer 1861 bracelet.

Hmm, actually the bracelet looks like the "Speedmaster" 020 bracelet? Let me consider: the links are five-row-ish, resembling the Omega 1171/633 bracelet. Actually there's a "flat link" bracelet with polished outer links... The image shows what appears to be a multi-row bracelet with brushed links.

Wait, this could be the Speedmaster Professional "Mitsukoshi" panda? No, it's black dial black bezel.

Key distinguishing: the "TACHYMÈTRE" bezel with dot-over-90 (Dot over 90 = DON bezel) — the image shows "500 400 300" etc. with tachymeter scale, and there's the dot over 90 visible near the 90 mark? The bezel at the top shows "500" at top right... Actually the tachymetre scale shown with "500" at ~12:30, "400, 300" going clockwise. And there's an accent appearing on the "90" mark — I see "9o" with a dot above? At around the 5 o'clock position on the bezel there's "90" and above it looks like there's a dot — hmm the image shows "9o" ... hard to tell.

The dial is black with white baton indices, three subdials. This is basically a standard Speedmaster Professional 3570.50.00 (cal 1861, hesalite crystal, stainless steel, 42mm) — with the 1998-onward dial with "OMEGA Speedmaster PROFESSIONAL" text.

But hold on — the subdial at 6 o'clock: standard Moonwatch has 12-hour counter with "12" at top, "6" bottom, "3" and "9" at sides. In the image: bottom subdial shows "12" at top and "6" at bottom, "9" at right? It shows "9" at bottom? Hmm. Let's just accept it's a Moonwatch.

Bracelet: the Moonwatch 3570.50.00 comes on the 1998-style bracelet. But wait, the photo shows a bracelet with narrow polished center links and flat links — could be the Speedmaster Professional bracelet ref 1998/1999? Or perhaps this is the "Speedmaster Professional 3573.50.00" (sapphire sandwich)? Not determinable.

However, the bracelet in the photo looks unusual — five-link? Let me look again: The bracelet shows three rows visible: outer rows brushed? It looks like a "Speedmaster" bracelet with three links: outer flat links and a center link? Actually there's a straight bar across the middle with polished link... Hmm, maybe it's a "1171" bracelet with 5 links.

Hmm actually looking at the photo: it looks like the bracelet has flat, wide links with a central polished strip? There's a distinct row of rectangular links in the middle and outer links slightly lower. This resembles the Speedmaster Professional "1863/1861" bracelet? Hmm.

Actually — wait. Perhaps this is a Speedmaster with a strap being a "JB Champion"? No.

Hmm — could this be the Omega Speedmaster Professional 3590.50? Or a Japan "Speedmaster Professional" with 1171 bracelet.

Alternatively, the bracelet could be an aftermarket "Forstner" flat-link bracelet which is common with the "Komi" look. The 1171 with 633 endlinks is the classic 1980s-90s Speedmaster bracelet.

Let me think about the bezel: The image shows the bezel with "TACHYMÈTRE" and the "dot over 90"? At the lower right on the bezel, I see what looks like "90" with a dot above it (or the "90" written as "9o" with the o above). That's the DON bezel used on vintage Speedmasters up to ~1969/70. But the dial with "PROFESSIONAL" and a modern look... Hmm, but there's also the modern re-edition 3590s.

Hmm, but the dial looks modern: white gold or applied indices? The main hands are white with luminous, the chrono hands white. Modern Moonwatch 3570.50.

Actually maybe it's a "Speedmaster Professional" with the "1957" style? No, that's a broad arrow.

I think the safest: Omega, Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch, reference 3570.50.00, manual, stainless steel, metal bracelet. Confidence maybe 0.4.

But wait — the bracelet: 3570.50.00 has the "1998" bracelet? Actually the 3570.50.00 (still in production until 2006?) came on the 1998/849 bracelet... The standard Moonwatch on steel bracelet has ref 3570.50.00 with the 1998 bracelet. Hmm, but this photo's bracelet has a flat-link look like the 1171. Hmm.

Actually hold on: Given it might have a "flat link" bracelet with polished center... Could this be the Speedmaster Professional 3570.50.00 with aftermarket bracelet? Or a Speedmaster Automatic "Reduced" 3510.50? No — the Reduced has subdials at 6, 9, 12.

Hmm, the caliber: it might be a "Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch" with hesalite. Alternatively it could be a "Speedmaster Professional 3572.50"? That's hesalite front sapphire back.

Could there be a Speedmaster with this "racing dial"? No, it's standard.

Another possible: This might be a Speedmaster Professional 145.022? No, it's modern-ish.

The dial has printed "OMEGA" with metal logo? It shows "OMEGA" applied in metal with "Speedmaster" and "PROFESSIONAL" printed. That's the 1990s+ dial.

I'll answer: brand Omega, model_family "Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch", reference "3570.50.00", movement manual, case_material stainless-steel, bracelet_material metal, confidence 0.35.

Hmm, but let me reconsider the bracelet: The 3570.50 comes with the professional bracelet ref 1998/849 (with polished center links? no, the 1998 bracelet is fully brushed with three links? The 1998 bracelet has brushed links and a polished strip? Hmm). Actually the classic Moonwatch bracelet (1998) has three-link design: outer links brushed, and the bracelet looks like the image? The image shows a bracelet with what appears to be 3-5 rows with brushed finish and a central raised link. That matches the 1998 bracelet reasonably.

Hmm — but actually the image's bracelet looks like the "Speedmaster" bracelet with flat links similar to the Seamaster 1450? I'll go with metal.

Alternatively, this could be the Speedmaster Professional 311.30.42.30.01.005 (the new 2015+ Moonwatch with 1861, hesalite, bracelet). But 3570.50.00's the classic. The dial details: the "new" dial of 311.30.42.30.01.005 is basically identical.

Given the photo appears recent (gloves, boxes), the watch could be a 311.30.42.30.01.005. But the bezel: the newer 005 has a "TACHYMÈTRE" with dot over 90? No, the new one has the "DON" style? The 2015 005 bezel is the standard matte with "Tachymètre" and dot next to 90? The 2015 Moonwatch bezel does NOT have dot over 90. The "DON" bezel is vintage.

In the photo I think I see near "90" the "9o" with a dot above the o — that would be "dot over 90". Hmm, and note the "500" at top left near start of scale? Actually in the image: at top "TACHYMÈTRE" then "500" then "400 300"? Wait at the top-right going down: 500, 400, 300, 275, 250, 220, 200, 190, 180, 170... typical.

The old DON bezel has "500" starting at 12 o'clock with the dot over 90. This photo — I'd say there's a chance this is a vintage 145.022 with DON bezel and 1171 bracelet? The dial looks too crisp.

Let me just guess 3570.50.00 with low confidence ~0.3. Actually, hold on: maybe it's a Speedmaster Professional 3570.50.00 — I'll go with it.

Hmm, wait — the subdial at 6 shows "12" at top; standard. Fine.

Alternatively maybe reference could be 145.0022 / 345.0022 (the same watch as vintage). But the "PROFESSIONAL" text under Speedmaster in italic script, modern.

Final answer.
